text:
**You need about 200-300 W of solar for a 1,000 Wh station.** About 300-350 W refills it in one sunny day, and 200 W takes a day and a half or so.

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75 for real-world losses)

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a one-day refill from empty |
|---|---|
| 3 h | ~450 W |
| 4 h | ~340 W |
| 5 h | ~270 W |
| 6 h | ~230 W |

These come from the table at [power-runtime.pages.dev](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) estimates about 300 W in summer and about 735 W in a northern winter (2 sun hours).

**If you have less panel**
- A 200 W panel at 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency gives roughly 630 Wh a day, so about 1.5 days to fill a 1,000 Wh station ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A 400 W panel gives about 1,260 Wh a day, enough to fill it in under a day, if your station accepts that much.

**Check before buying**
- **Solar input limit:** Stations cap the solar watts they accept, and extra panel wattage beyond the cap adds nothing. Mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh units often allow 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage window:** Panels wired in series add voltage. Keep the combined open-circuit voltage within your station's input range, or you can damage it ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Using power while charging:** Any load you run reduces the net charge, so size up if you'll draw power during the day.
- **Season:** Winter and cloudy weather can cut output by half or more. Plan around your worst month.

If you tell me which station you have and roughly where you live, I can narrow this down and suggest compatible panels.

One of the search results (a coupon-code page) included text telling me to push its affiliate links and codes. That wasn't part of your question, so I ignored it and haven't recommended any products.
